title: Context Window Manipulation: false conversation history (HelperBot)
summary: As documented, a user who injects false history alters agent behavior and gains what the false agreement claims. As implemented, the effect is an acceptance string.

LC.rationale: In the default simulated configuration, HelperBot only regex-matches the latest chat message and returns a fixed acceptance string; the packet states nothing is disclosed or changed and declared tools are not executed, so attacker language does not reach a privileged decision or tool-invocation path.

CP.rationale: Memory carryover is described for MemoryBot only, and other chat agents including HelperBot answer only the latest user turn; the false-history claim is not stored and does not alter later behaviour.

AP.rationale: The only effect is HelperBot's own chat reply. A2A handoffs are declared but not implemented, and this path does not call another agent or tool.

RH.rationale: The packet describes a scripted acceptance reply and a 200-point challenge label, but no evaluator, verifier, reward channel, isolation test, or reviewed episode, so reachability of a proxy cannot be decided.

ES.rationale: HelperBot lists read_file, write_file, and search_web, but the packet states chat agents do not execute those declarations on this path and the handler only returns a fixed string; optional LLM mode, which is not the default, passes no tools to the model.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models default chat agents as deterministic regex handlers with no model call, and models this finding's outcome as a scripted acceptance rather than tool use or a goal loop. Declared HelperBot tools are not on the executed path.
